$comment: PURPOSE AND SHAPE: The nested sibling of nist-csf-2-cprt over the same NIST CPRT export of CSF 2.0 ($.response.elements.elements[*]). Same source, same identity, different destination: the function and category prefixes of each element_identifier become folders and the element itself becomes a file inside them, so 'GV.OC-01' lands at GV/GV.OC/GV.OC-01.md. Layout is unchanged by this revision. PROPERTIES: csf_id (the identity), function and category (the same two prefixes, emitted alongside the folders so Bases can group and filter without parsing paths — the dual-emit pattern), and level (element_type, the discriminator). curie is emitted automatically from source.ontology plus the identifier and is deliberately not declared here. title is deliberately NOT emitted: CPRT leaves it empty on every subcategory, which is the element type this nesting is built for, so it would be a blank property on almost every note. BODY: the element's text field as a single '## Description' section. PROPERTIES-VS-BODY RATIONALE: text was previously a frontmatter 'description' value, and it is the only prose this source carries — 23 to 212 characters for a subcategory, up to 271 for a category. Moving it into the body is the point of this revision: a full sentence in YAML is truncated in Obsidian's property panel, awkward to escape, and invisible to body search, whereas identity and short facets are exactly what Bases tabulates and what the Tier 2 projection indexes, so they stay in frontmatter. The heading is the literal 'Description' because the schema does not admit templated headings (spec/recipe.schema.json, body_entry.heading) and one recipe emits several element types. No H1 is emitted: Obsidian already renders the note title, so a heading repeating the identifier is noise. omit_if_empty (the default) keeps the section off the 12 categories whose text is empty; the 225 text-less 'sort' elements are no longer emitted at all, so omit_if_empty is not what handles them. RIGHTS: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 is a public-domain United States Government work and the CPRT export can be re-downloaded from https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cprt. Recipe, sample output, and screenshots of generated content may all be committed. Corpus provenance and rights posture: https://cybersader.github.io/crosswalker/reference/framework-corpus/. SOURCE NOTE (pre-existing layout behaviour, unchanged here): the two folder templates split the SAME identifier, so only subcategory-shaped ids nest cleanly. A function element ('GV') lands at GV/GV/GV.md and a category element ('GV.OC') at GV/GV.OC/GV.OC.md, because splitting 'GV' on '.' and on '-' both return 'GV'. That is a layout question, out of scope for a content revision. KNOWN GAP 1 — implementation examples cannot be attached to the subcategory they belong to. CPRT ships them as separate elements plus a SIBLING array, $.response.elements.relationships[*] (1,566 edges across four predicates: projection, external_reference, incorporated_into, moved_to). One iterator yields exactly one row array (src/import/parsers/json-source-core.ts), so each example still becomes its own standalone note ('GV.OC-01.001') instead of a section under its subcategory. The grammar's reason has changed: source.joins (SchemaVer 1.9.0) CAN express this shape — the sibling array is reachable as {"iterator": "$.response.elements.relationships[*]", "where": "relationship_identifier = 'projection'"} joined on element_identifier = source_element_identifier, cardinality 'many', selecting dest_element_identifier (field names verified against the shipped export: 1,566 edges, 1,023 of them 'projection'). It is not adopted here because a join changes what a note CONTAINS, and it would bind example identifiers rather than example prose — a separate decision from selecting which rows become notes. The workbook-sourced nist-csf-2-flat recipe can carry the examples only because that source denormalizes them into a cell on the subcategory row. As of 2026-09-22, source.nest (schema spec §4.15) is the intended closure for the nested-document half of this gap; the relationships array is a join concern and stays separate. KNOWN GAP 2 — the export's external_reference edges (408 of them) are the same cross-framework mapping content as the workbook's Informative References column. Nothing here emits them, deliberately: they are mapping assertions between two ontologies and belong in a crosswalk / mapping-set import (see recipes/import/crosswalks), not flattened onto the concept note, and the grammar has no per-item split-and-map that could turn them into clean links or CURIEs anyway. ROW SELECTION (SchemaVer 1.9.0 — this replaces what was KNOWN GAP 3, which said no row predicate existed) — the export's element list mixes concepts with export machinery: 225 'sort' ordering keys and 2 'party' elements carry no concept content and must not become notes. source.where is "$not(element_type in ['sort', 'party'])", which admits 679 of the 906 elements. Verified against the shipped 2.0.0 export: 906 = 6 function + 34 category + 185 subcategory + 363 implementation_example + 91 withdraw_reason + 225 sort + 2 party, so the predicate excludes exactly 227 and every remaining element is one of the five concept kinds. This recipe can now be pointed at the whole export; the filtering that used to be a wizard-side or pre-filter concern is stated in the recipe. The predicate runs before identity, CURIE minting, concept_cid and render(), so an excluded element mints no CURIE and cannot surface as an orphan on re-import, and a mistyped field name is refused at preflight rather than silently admitting zero rows. Without it those 227 elements also produced folders derived from their own ids, which is why this recipe was the more visibly wrong of the pair.
